title: Real-Time Chat (WhatsApp / Messenger)
summary: Deliver messages the instant they're sent, with presence and durable history, across a fleet of servers.
narrative:
Chat is fundamentally bidirectional. Frequent polling wastes requests and adds delay — the moment a message arrives it has to be pushed to the recipient. Long polling is an alternative, but here use persistent connections: WebSockets that stay open so either side can send at any time.

The hard part is that a million users don't all land on the same server. When Alice, connected to server A, messages Bob, connected to server B, server A has to get that message across to server B. A Pub/Sub layer solves this: each server subscribes to the channels for the users it holds, and any server can publish to fan a message out to whichever server owns the recipient. A cache tracks presence — who is online and which server currently holds their connection — so routing stays fast. For small groups, fan out on write to each member; assign per-conversation sequence numbers so each device can resume from its last acknowledged message and keep sent/delivered/read receipts consistent.

Messages also have to survive. Enqueue durably before acknowledging a send, then persist history asynchronously to NoSQL; the Queue → NoSQL edge models that persistence consumer. Retry with message ids for deduplication, and let offline devices catch up by sequence number after reconnecting. A separate queue consumer (Worker) invokes the Notification Service for APNs/FCM push when recipients are offline; push alerts are best effort and do not replace durable history. Online delivery targets < 100 ms; offline push is a slower background branch.

functional: Deliver messages in real time over persistent connections
Fan a message out to a recipient on any server
Track who is online and where they're connected
Track sent/delivered/read receipts and per-conversation sequence numbers across devices
Fan out small-group messages on write and notify offline recipients through APNs/FCM
nonFunctional: Online message delivery under 100 ms at p99; offline push runs asynchronously
Durably acknowledged messages survive restarts; retries deduplicate by message id
Survive the loss of any single WebSocket server
constraints: Clients connect only through the load balancer
History is written off the delivery hot path
specs.tradeoff: Durable enqueue adds an acknowledgement step while history persistence and offline push run asynchronously. WebSockets minimize online delivery delay; long polling is a fallback with more request overhead. Small-group fan-out on write speeds reads at the cost of per-recipient work.
specs.bonus: Add Monitoring to track connection counts, fan-out lag, and queue depth.

missions.label: Connect clients through the Load Balancer
Route connections to a WebSocket Server
Fan messages out across servers via Pub/Sub
Track presence and connection routing in the Cache
Persist message history to the NoSQL store
Consume offline delivery jobs with a Worker
Send offline recipients an APNs/FCM push via the Notification Service

topologyRules.message: Connections must enter through the Load Balancer, not straight to a WebSocket server.
Clients must never read the history store directly.
History access must go through the WebSocket tier and its persistence pipeline.

resilienceRules.message: Run at least two WebSocket servers so a single failure doesn't drop every open connection.
Cross-server delivery needs Pub/Sub to fan messages out to whichever server holds the recipient.

hints: Clients hold a persistent connection: Client → Load Balancer → WebSocket Server. Run at least two WebSocket servers so no single failure disconnects everyone.
Connect the WebSocket servers to Pub/Sub so a message from one server reaches a recipient on any other, and use the Cache for presence and connection routing.

Wire Message Queue → NoSQL Database for history persistence and Message Queue → Worker → Notification Service for offline push. Connect Monitoring to the WebSocket tier; use sequence numbers and message ids for catch-up and retry deduplication.
tips: How do you ensure low-latency message delivery (< 100ms) across millions of users?
What communication protocol will you use (long polling, WebSockets)?
How do you handle offline users and guarantee eventual delivery?
Where do you store messages - do you persist all, or support auto-deletion?
How will you implement push notifications on iOS/Android reliably?
How do you support multi-device sync (message states consistent across devices)?
How will you manage group messaging - fan-out on write vs fan-out on read?
